name: "Tuna Melt" Quesadillas & Tomato-Carrot Soup with Parsley

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 medium carrots
3 sticks celery
1 small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince garlic; peel and small dice onions. Place both in a medium bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 cloves garlic
1 ½ medium yellow onions

instructions.primary_message: Peel and coarsely grate carrots. Add to the bowl with the garlic and onion.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.

Once the pot is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic, onion, carrot, and spices to the pot; cook, stirring often, until veggies begin to soften, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp butter, unsalted
1 ½ tsp Italian seasoning
1 ½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, mince capers. Place in the reserved bowl along with mayo, vinegar, cumin, and pepper; stir to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tbsp capers
⅓ cup mayonnaise
¾ tsp red wine vinegar
¾ tsp cumin, ground
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add tomatoes, broth, and sugar to the pot; stir to combine and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and let simmer until veggies are completely soft, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (398 ml) cans diced tomatoes
1065 ml chicken or vegetable broth
1 ½ tsp brown sugar

instructions.primary_message: While the soup is cooking, drain tuna; flake into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the mayo mixture (do not mash).
instructions.secondary_message: 3 (170 g) cans chunk light tuna in water

instructions.primary_message: Trim, and small dice celery. Add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl (reserving the rest for the soup).
Grate cheese and add to the bowl; gently stir to combine the tuna filling.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide the tuna filling between them. Move the filling onto one half of each tortilla; fold in half to close.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches, add quesadillas and cook, flipping once, until cheese is melted and tortillas are golden, 1½-2 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, using a hand (or regular) blender, purée the soup until smooth. Alternatively, use a potato masher to crush the tomatoes (the soup will be chunkier).
Divide soup between bowls and sprinkle with reserved parsley. Serve with quesadillas on the side and enjoy!
